1_PORT_MANAGEMENT.priority: HIGHEST - CHECK THIS FIRST EVERY SESSION
1_PORT_MANAGEMENT.rule: NEVER use individual npm run dev commands - ALWAYS use the unified start-dev.sh script
1_PORT_MANAGEMENT.why: Individual commands cause port conflicts, lingering processes, and consumed tokens on restarts
correct_procedure: 1️⃣  Check if services running: lsof -i :3000,:3001,:8000 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN
2️⃣  If YES: killall -9 node npm python3 && sleep 3
4️⃣  WAIT for output: 'All Services Started Successfully! 🚀'
5️⃣  FRONTEND ALWAYS ON PORT 3000 - script now ensures this with explicit -p 3000 flag
6️⃣  VERIFY with: lsof -i :3000-3010 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN | awk '{print $9}' | sort -u
WRONG_APPROACH_DO_NOT_USE: ❌ cd backend && npm run dev &  (causes port 3001 conflicts)
❌ cd frontend && npm run dev & (causes port conflicts, wrong ports)
❌ Assuming frontend auto-increments (it now locks to 3000)

1b_FRONTEND_PORT_LOCKING.priority: CRITICAL - Frontend MUST ALWAYS be on port 3000
1b_FRONTEND_PORT_LOCKING.rule: Frontend is locked to port 3000 with explicit -p 3000 flag. Never let it auto-increment to 3003, 3005, 5000, etc.
1b_FRONTEND_PORT_LOCKING.why: Frontend on inconsistent ports breaks API integration, causes confusion, wastes tokens on port debugging
implementation: ✅ start-dev.sh now clears port 3000 FIRST before starting frontend
✅ start-dev.sh passes explicit '-p 3000' flag to 'npm run dev'
✅ If port 3000 still in use: run 'lsof -ti :3000 | xargs kill -9' before start-dev.sh

what_this_means.if_3000_occupied: Kill the process: lsof -ti :3000 | xargs kill -9 && sleep 2 && ./start-dev.sh

2_PROMPT_REFINEMENT.priority: HIGHEST - DO THIS BEFORE ANY WORK
steps: 1. STOP - Do NOT start coding immediately
2. Read this settings.json file (especially PORT_MANAGEMENT rule above)
3. Check PROJECT_CONTEXT.md for related Known Issues & Fixes
5. Show structured prompt to user with context references

mandatory: Apply Prompt Refinement Layer (see this file, then PROJECT_CONTEXT.md)
After ANY code change: Use ./start-dev.sh, detect actual ports, provide correct links

beforeAnyCode: Show user structured prompt with context and ask for confirmation

afterAnyCodeChange.CRITICAL: Use ./start-dev.sh script - NEVER individual npm commands
afterAnyCodeChange.step1: Check if services running: lsof -i :3000,:3001,:8000 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN
afterAnyCodeChange.step2: If running: killall -9 node npm python3 2>/dev/null && sleep 3
afterAnyCodeChange.step3: RUN UNIFIED SCRIPT: ./start-dev.sh (wait for '✅ All Services Started Successfully! 🚀')
afterAnyCodeChange.step4: DETECT actual ports: lsof -i :3000-3010 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN | awk '{print $9}' | sort -u
afterAnyCodeChange.step5: Provide correct localhost links based on actual script output (check Next.js port - may be 3000, 3003, 3005+)

links.frontend: http://localhost:[PORT] - GET PORT FROM SCRIPT OUTPUT
links.note: Do NOT assume frontend is 3002 or 3003 - check actual script output

afterAnyCodeChange.verification: Show user the actual ports from script output + lsof command so they know for certain
